_what: THE ADMISSION SET: which registered verdict types must be green for gitRobot to let an action through. This is NOT the registry. The registry (verdictLedger's required.v2.json) says what may be RECORDED; this says what must PASS. Twenty experimental gates recording while three admit a push is a coherent, intended state.
_why_here: Separation of duty. The ledger records verdicts; if it also decided what was SUFFICIENT, anyone able to edit ledger config could lower the bar that admits a push in one place. Split them and two systems must agree before the bar moves. This is a deliberate, NARROW reversal of 'no policy values in gitRobot' -- the type registry, min_passes, max_depth, lock waits, the genesis floor and HOW `complete` is computed all stay in the ledger, and gitRobot never re-derives completeness. It names this set and requires the ledger's answer.
_explicit_not_defaulted: A type gates because it is NAMED here, never because it exists. The alternative -- every registered type gates by default -- forces a correct implementation to block every push until every registered type has an emitter, and a model whose correct implementation bricks the system is describing the wrong system.
_the_cost_and_its_control: An explicit list reintroduces the hazard the registry header warns about: a finished gate nobody promotes never gates, silently. That is paid for by the ledger printing `registered_not_admitting` on EVERY allow and EVERY refusal, so a promotion gap is visible on every run rather than discovered a year later. Same principle as a downgraded gate having to get louder.
_empty_REFUSES_it_is_not_legitimate: An EMPTY list for an action REFUSES that action on the main repo. It does not allow-with-a-warning. This was the second half of the 2026-08-23 failure and the subtler half: the first build of this gate rendered EMPTY as ALLOWED plus a loud capitalised warning, which is fail-OPEN in the costume of fail-closed -- a warning nobody is obliged to act on gates nothing. Tim: "It should have been impossible to push without having the preset of requirements from verdictLedger created." An empty set IS that preset not existing.
_the_consequence_is_intended: As of 2026-08-23 no ZeroParadox checker calls record.py, so `push` on the main repo is BLOCKED until a type is promoted here AND something records it. That is the point: the system should be unusable in exactly the state where it cannot tell you whether anything was checked. The refusal names the registered types available to promote, so the way out is discoverable without reading this file. `.claude-local` is unaffected -- it has no pipeline and never reaches the gate.
_which_is_still_explicit_not_defaulted: Note this does NOT mean every registered type gates by default. A type gates because it is NAMED here. The empty-set refusal is a floor on the LIST BEING EMPTY, not an implicit promotion of everything in the registry -- those are different, and conflating them would brick the push path with checks nobody chose.
